name: Giant Rhinoceros Beetle
appearance: A twelve-foot beetle with a horn about six feet long and a frequently bright or iridescent shell.

Attacks.name: Mandibles and horn
Attacks.effectNote: The mandibles deal 3d6 damage, and the single horn deals 2d8 damage.

Habitat and behavior.name: Jungle forager
Habitat and behavior.effectNote: It looks for fruit and vegetation in the rain forest and may crush obstacles in its path.

notes: 1–6 appearing. Uncommon. The table lists solitary organization and any activity cycle.
Nonintelligent (0). Neutral. Treasure, special attacks, special defenses and magic resistance Nil. No fixed HP.
Monstrous Manual, TSR 2140, third printing (January 1994), pp. 18–19.

name: Giant Stag Beetle
appearance: A ten-foot beetle with two long horns, usually each at least eight feet long.

Attacks.name: Paired horns
Attacks.effectNote: The table gives a first attack for 4–16 damage and one attack with each horn for 1–10. The text identifies the horns and leaves the first attack unnamed.

Habitat and behavior.name: Crop raids
Habitat and behavior.effectNote: It feeds chiefly on grain and other crops. A raid can strip a farm and stampede livestock. A hungry Stag Beetle may also eat livestock.

notes: 2–12 appearing. Common. The table lists solitary organization and any activity cycle.
The table lists Herbivore. Elite (13) morale.
Nonintelligent (0). Neutral. Treasure, special attacks, special defenses and magic resistance Nil. No fixed HP.
Monstrous Manual, TSR 2140, third printing (January 1994), pp. 18–19.

name: Giant Water Beetle
appearance: A six-foot air-breathing beetle that carries a bubble under its wings.

habitats: Fresh water at least 30 feet deep

Habitat and behavior.name: Freshwater hunter
Habitat and behavior.effectNote: It hunts by scent and by feeling vibrations. Water beetles sometimes attack and sink vessels on rivers and lakes. The source gives no separate vessel attack or damage values.

Habitat and behavior.name: Air bubble
Habitat and behavior.effectNote: It carries air under its wings to stay underwater for extended periods and can release a bubble into a cave or other cavity that will hold it. The description gives no duration.

notes: 1–12 appearing. Common. The table lists solitary organization and any activity cycle.
